title: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: A slow-simmered tomato sauce, a little patience, and a generous shower of Parmesan. Sunday comfort, any day of the week.
instructions: Finely chop the onion and garlic. Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, then the beef. Break it up with a spoon and cook until browned throughout.
Stir in the tomatoes and 100 ml water. Season to taste and simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water according to the packet. Drain, reserving a little cooking water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, loosening with cooking water if needed. Serve with grated Parmesan.

title: Blueberry Pancakes
description: Fluffy golden stacks with juicy blueberries tucked into every bite. Slow mornings start here.
instructions: Mix the flour and baking powder in a bowl with a pinch of salt.
Whisk the milk and egg together, then stir into the dry ingredients just until combined. Fold in the blueberries.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Spoon in small rounds of batter.
Cook until bubbles appear and the edges set, then flip. Cook for another 1–2 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

title: Pumpkin Soup
description: Silky, warming, and bright as autumn. A simple pot of comfort with a toasted-seed finish.
instructions: Peel the pumpkin and cut into small cubes. Dice the onion and chop the garlic.
Heat the oil in a saucepan. Soften the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and pumpkin.
Pour in the stock. Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until the pumpkin is soft.
Let cool slightly, then blend until smooth. Stir in the cream and reheat gently.
Season to taste and finish with pumpkin seeds.

title: Caprese Salad
description: Ripe tomatoes, soft mozzarella, and fragrant basil. Proof that good ingredients need very little fuss.
instructions: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella into rounds.
Arrange them on a platter, alternating tomato and mozzarella. Tuck basil leaves between the slices.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper and serve immediately.

title: Vegetable Curry
description: A colorful one-pot curry with coconut milk and soft chickpeas. Weeknight-friendly and wonderfully generous.
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet. Drain the chickpeas and dice the vegetables.
Heat the oil in a deep pan and soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the curry powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the carrots, pepper, chickpeas, and coconut milk. Add a splash of water if needed.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes until the vegetables are tender. Season to taste.
Serve over the rice, spooning plenty of sauce into each bowl.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Crisp edges, soft middles, and chocolate in all the right places. Save a few for tomorrow. Maybe.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a baking tray. Soften the butter.
Beat the butter and sugar until creamy. Mix in the egg and vanilla.
Fold in the flour and baking powder, then the chocolate chips.
Spoon 12 small mounds onto the tray, leaving room to spread. Bake for 10–12 minutes until the edges are golden.
Leave on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack. This batch makes 12 cookies, or 6 servings of two cookies.

title: Tomato Basil Bruschetta
description: Crunchy toast, bright tomatoes, and a whisper of garlic. A little sunshine on a plate.
instructions: Dice the tomatoes and tear the basil. Toss with half the olive oil and season to taste.
Toast or grill the bread until golden on both sides.
Cut the garlic clove in half and lightly rub over the warm toast.
Spoon the tomato mixture over the bread, drizzle with the remaining oil, and serve straight away.

title: Teriyaki Tofu Bowl
description: Sticky glazed tofu, crisp greens, and fluffy rice. A bowl worth slowing down for.
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet. Press the tofu dry and cut into cubes.
Mix the soy sauce, brown sugar, chopped garlic, and 2 tablespoons of water.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan. Brown the tofu on each side, then pour in the sauce.
Simmer for 2–3 minutes until the sauce coats the tofu. Steam the broccoli until tender-crisp.
Divide the rice and broccoli between bowls and top with the glazed tofu.
